# Template allow-list — the hosts and networks every container built from this
# template needs. Read by init-firewall.sh before firewall-allow.txt.
#
# DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE TO GIVE ONE PROJECT ACCESS TO SOMETHING.
# That is what .devcontainer/firewall-allow.txt is for. This file is
# boilerplate: it is overwritten when the devcontainer is refreshed from
# DEV-TEMPLATE, and an edit here is lost at that point.
#
# Format, identical in both files:
#   - one entry per line: a domain name, a bare IPv4 address, or an IPv4 CIDR
#   - `#` starts a comment, to end of line; blank lines are ignored
#   - domains are resolved at boot and every A record is added to the ipset
#
# Entries here are FAIL-CLOSED: anything that does not resolve or does not
# parse aborts container start, because a container missing npm or the
# Anthropic API is not usefully "started". Project entries are best-effort by
# contrast — see firewall-allow.txt.
#
# GitHub is deliberately absent: its ranges are fetched live from
# api.github.com/meta, which is authoritative and far wider than DNS would give.
#
# herdr.dev is deliberately absent. install-herdr.sh runs at create time,
# before postStartCommand raises the firewall, so the download needs no entry,
# and the release asset it fetches is on GitHub in any case. Once the firewall
# is up, `herdr update` cannot reach herdr.dev — that is the version pin
# working, not a fault.

# --- Language package registries -------------------------------------------
# npm and PyPI cover the Node and Python features this template ships on.
registry.npmjs.org
pypi.org
files.pythonhosted.org

# --- Claude Code -----------------------------------------------------------
api.anthropic.com

# --- Ubuntu archives -------------------------------------------------------
# What makes `sudo apt-get install` work in a RUNNING container. Without these,
# apt only works before the firewall comes up (onCreateCommand) and every later
# install hangs on the connect — which reads as a broken mirror rather than as
# the policy doing its job, on a base image whose whole point is that projects
# add what they need.
#
# archive/security cover amd64; ports.ubuntu.com is the arm64 archive, so on
# Apple Silicon that is the one actually used. All three are listed because the
# template runs on both.
#
# Worth knowing: these are round-robin mirror pools with more addresses than one
# A lookup returns, so the boot-time snapshot can miss the host apt later picks.
# That is the staleness the whole domain mechanism has; the answer is the same,
# re-run init-firewall.sh.
archive.ubuntu.com
security.ubuntu.com
ports.ubuntu.com

# --- VS Code Server and telemetry ------------------------------------------
marketplace.visualstudio.com
vscode.blob.core.windows.net
update.code.visualstudio.com
sentry.io
statsig.com

# --- LAN networks ----------------------------------------------------------
# The LAN segment the local LLM lives on — the endpoint opencode is pointed at
# via OPENAI_BASE_URL in devcontainer.json. It is NOT reachable through the
# host-network rule in the script: that is derived from the default route, which
# inside the container is the Docker bridge gateway (172.x), not the LAN.
#
# A literal CIDR involves no DNS, so unlike a domain it cannot fail a boot.
192.168.12.0/24
